sections.title: Systems Biology of Cell Signaling Behavior
sections.description: This course discusses the principles of cell signaling and cell decisions. We start from a molecular description of cell signaling components. The course builds towards understanding how their interactions govern cell and tissue behavior and how these processes can breakdown in disease. We conclude with a survey of modern approaches to analyze and manipulate signaling networks to study and control biological systems. Graduate, Junior or Senior standing in Bioengineering or permission of the instructor.

sections.title: Systems Biology of Cell Signaling Behavior
sections.description: This course discusses the principles of cell signaling and how these principles can be harnessed to engineer novel protein and cellular functions. We start from a molecular description of cell signaling components and build towards understanding how their interactions govern cell and tissue behavior both in health and disease. Discussions integrate how systems and synthetic biology can harness molecular principles of signaling for a variety of fundamental, biomedical, and biotechnological aims. Critical reading of current literature reinforces and expands on lecture topics. Open to graduate students or undergraduates with senior standing by permission of instructor.
